note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 3 October 1946. Nominations were complete by 26 September, when the Impartial Reporter printed the uncontested seats and the changes of personnel (p. 5). The only contest was Garvary, where the outgoing Unionist held the seat by eight votes. Doagh drew no nomination and the retiring Nationalist, Mr. Charles Murphy, remained in office. The paper records changes at Tempo, Ballyreagh, Kinawley, Clabby, Drumderg, Drummully (printed for Drummee), Lisbellaw and Corryglass; the other uncontested members are recorded where a selection list or a report of the new council's meetings names them, each division inferred from the 1939 return. The paper notes no change in the political complexion of the council. Filled from the Impartial Reporter's lists of Unionist candidates (22 and 29 August 1946, p. 5), where the selected candidate is the member previously carried: Castlecoole, Rahalton, Enniskillen Rural, Coolyermor, Lisbofin and Killesher. Recorded from reports of the new council's meetings during the term: Drumane, Kinglass, Oldbarr and Newporton. Holywell: a by-election in July 1947 returned Patrick James Timoney (Returning Officer's notice dated 29 July 1947, Fermanagh Herald, 2 August 1947, p. 4); recorded as a note only. Printed 'Hon. C. L.-Corry'; the earlier record carried 'Hon. Cecil Lowry-Corry' from the 1939 return. Returned unopposed.
